newsitem.title: USA: US comptroller concerned about syndicated loans.
newsitem.headline: US comptroller concerned about syndicated loans.

text.p: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said Tuesday he is concerned that banks have relaxed lending standards on syndicated loans.

"In some credit areas, underwriting standards continue to erode and have eroded to a point where there is not much farther they can go and remain prudent," Ludwig said in remarks prepared for delivery to a Robert Morris Associates conference here.
"An area where we are seeing this disturbing trend is the syndicated credit market," he said.
Bank examiners from Ludwig's office have found some loans where the pricing "does not appear to adequately reflect risk," the comptroller said.

Strong demand for high yielding loans is driving underwriting standards lower, Ludwig said. "We are also seeing, in some cases, investors willing to accept inferior standards simply to stay in the market," he said.
Senior bank management should carefully reassess existing underwriting standards and the nature of exceptions permitted, Ludwig said.
Ludwig also warned banks not to be pressured by tight deadlines into lowering their standards.
"When there is not sufficient time to engage in an independent credit analysis, the bank should be prepared to decline the deal," Ludwig said.
